headings.title: Judgment for or against multiple parties and determination of rights
headings.reviewNote: Permits judgment for or against multiple plaintiffs or defendants, determination of ultimate rights between parties on each side, and grant of affirmative relief.

headings.title: Court authorization of care arrangements for minor or disabled person
headings.reviewNote: Permits court in judgment, without appointing a conservator, to authorize, direct, or ratify chapter 475 care, security, or service arrangements for a minor or disabled party.

headings.title: Court approval of financial transactions for minor or disabled person
headings.reviewNote: Permits court in judgment, without appointing a conservator, to authorize, direct, or ratify best-interests chapter 475 financial or estate transactions for a minor or disabled party.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections and statutory history; permissive judgment relief and chapter 475 minor/disabled party care and financial transaction powers verified.

headings.title: Recording requirement for real estate judgments within eight months
headings.reviewNote: Requires prevailing party to record a copy of a final real estate conveyance or quiet-title judgment in the county recorder's office within eight months.

headings.title: Effect of unrecorded judgment and extended petition for review
headings.reviewNote: Renders unrecorded real estate judgment invalid except between parties and those with actual notice, extends defendant's review-petition period to two years and four months after recording, and preserves section 511.180.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; eight-month county recording requirement, unrecorded-judgment invalidity, extended review-petition period, and section 511.180 proviso verified.

headings.title: Courts of record judgment liens on county real estate
headings.reviewNote: Establishes county real estate liens for judgments of designated courts of record, excluding associate, small claims, and municipal divisions of circuit courts.

headings.title: Filing requirement for associate circuit court judgment liens
headings.reviewNote: Provides that associate circuit division judgments do not become real estate liens until filed with the circuit clerk under sections 517.141 and 517.151.

headings.title: No real estate liens for small claims and municipal judgments
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that small claims and municipal division judgments do not constitute liens against real estate.

headings.title: Prohibition on administrative amendment of court judgments
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits administrative agencies from amending or modifying court judgments or decrees without approval of a court of competent jurisdiction.

headings.title: Court approval required for administrative child support modifications
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits administrative agencies, notwithstanding subsection 4 or other law, from amending or modifying court child support orders without court approval.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 5 subsections and statutory history; court-of-record real estate liens, associate-circuit filing rule, small-claims/municipal exclusions, and administrative-modification prohibitions verified.

headings.title: Transcript filing and lien creation in another county
headings.reviewNote: Creates a real estate lien in another county upon filing and indexing a transcript of a qualifying court-of-record judgment with that county's circuit clerk.

headings.title: Recording and indexing requirements for transcript of judgment
headings.reviewNote: Requires entry of the transcript in the circuit clerk's judgment record under section 511.500 for a county or city not within a county, including the rendering court's name and location.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; out-of-county transcript lien creation and circuit clerk entry requirements under section 511.500 verified.

headings.title: Execution and revival powers of court where transcript filed
headings.reviewNote: Deems sections 511.460 to 511.480 to authorize the court where a transcript is filed to issue executions, conduct debtor proceedings, and issue scire facias to revive the judgment or lien.

headings.title: Limitation on execution and revival for section 511.440 transcripts
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits courts where section 511.440 judgment transcripts are filed from issuing executions or scire facias, requiring issuance from the original rendering court.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, statutory history, and catchline-vs-body note (catchline retains historical magistrate-judgment phrasing while body distinguishes sections 511.460 to 511.480 from section 511.440 transcripts).

headings.title: Definitions for uniform enforcement of foreign judgments
headings.reviewNote: Defines foreign judgment, judgment debtor, levy, and register for purposes of this section.

headings.title: Application to register foreign judgment
headings.reviewNote: Permits a person entitled to sue on a foreign judgment to register it in a Missouri court with jurisdiction within the allowed action period.

headings.title: Petition contents and notification of original rendering court
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes contents of an authenticated verified registration petition and requires the registering clerk to notify the original rendering court's clerk.

headings.title: Issuance and service of summons on judgment debtor
headings.reviewNote: Entitles petitioner after registration to have summons issued and served on the judgment debtor in any manner authorized for personal jurisdiction.

headings.title: Notice by mail when personal jurisdiction unavailable
headings.reviewNote: Requires the registering clerk to send notice by registered mail to the debtor's last known address when personal jurisdiction cannot be obtained, with clerk certificate as proof.

headings.title: Levy on property under registered judgment prior to final judgment
headings.reviewNote: Permits levy on debtor property subject to execution at any time after registration regardless of personal jurisdiction or final judgment.

headings.title: Final personal judgment upon failure to plead or after hearing
headings.reviewNote: Converts registered judgment into a final personal judgment if debtor fails to plead within thirty days after personal jurisdiction or after court refuses to set aside registration.

headings.title: Defenses, setoffs, counterclaims, and pleading deadlines
headings.reviewNote: Permits assertion of state-law defenses, setoffs, and counterclaims within thirty days after personal jurisdiction or thirty-five days after subsection 5 mailing.

headings.title: Stay of trial and relief from levy pending foreign appeal
headings.reviewNote: Requires court to postpone trial on just terms when debtor shows a pending or intended foreign appeal, and permits setting aside levy upon adequate security.

headings.title: Order setting aside registration constitutes final judgment
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that an order setting aside a registration constitutes a final judgment in favor of the judgment debtor.

headings.title: Appellate review of orders sustaining or setting aside registration
headings.reviewNote: Permits either party to appeal a judgment or order sustaining or setting aside registration on the same terms as other appeals from that court.

headings.title: Final judgment quasi in rem binding levied property
headings.reviewNote: Directs entry of a final judgment quasi in rem binding levied property if personal jurisdiction is not secured within thirty days of levy and debtor does not act within thirty-five days of notice.

headings.title: Execution sale under levy and distribution of proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Permits execution sale after final personal or quasi in rem judgment (except as provided for perishable goods) with sale and proceeds distribution under Missouri law.

headings.title: Inclusion of foreign interest, copy costs, and court costs
headings.reviewNote: Requires final judgment to include interest under rendering-state law, authenticated copy costs, and incidental Missouri court costs.

headings.title: Satisfaction of foreign judgment in other jurisdictions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that partial or complete satisfaction of the original judgment or another state's judgment operates as satisfaction in Missouri except for subsection 14 costs.

headings.title: Preservation of separate action on foreign judgment
headings.reviewNote: Preserves unimpaired a judgment creditor's right to bring a separate action to enforce the judgment instead of proceeding under this section.

headings.title: Uniformity of interpretation and construction
headings.reviewNote: Directs uniform interpretation and construction of this section among enacting states.

headings.title: Short title citation
headings.reviewNote: Permits citation of this section as the Uniform Enforcement of Foreign Judgments Law.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 18 subsections, statutory history, and 5 case annotations; tightened subsections 14 and 16 to match exact statutory wording ('authenticated copy' and separate enforcement action) and verified mandatory vs permissive rules.

headings.title: Short title citation
headings.reviewNote: Permits citation of sections 511.770 to 511.787 as the Uniform Foreign Country Money-Judgments Recognition Act.

headings.title: Uniformity of interpretation and construction
headings.reviewNote: Directs construction of sections 511.770 to 511.787 to effectuate uniformity among enacting states.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; permissive short-title citation and uniform construction directive for sections 511.770 to 511.787 verified.

headings.title: Mandatory grounds for nonrecognition of foreign country judgment
headings.reviewNote: Lists three mandatory grounds on which a foreign country judgment is not conclusive: lack of impartial/due-process system, lack of personal jurisdiction, or lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.

headings.title: Discretionary grounds for nonrecognition of foreign country judgment
headings.reviewNote: Lists six discretionary grounds on which a foreign country judgment need not be recognized, including insufficient notice, fraud, public-policy repugnancy, conflicting judgment, contrary dispute agreement, or seriously inconvenient forum.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; mandatory nonconclusiveness grounds (subsection 1) and discretionary nonrecognition grounds (subsection 2) verified.

headings.title: Recognized bases of personal jurisdiction for foreign judgment
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits refusing recognition for lack of personal jurisdiction when any of six specified jurisdictional contacts or agreements applies.

headings.title: Recognition of other jurisdictional bases consistent with fairness
headings.reviewNote: Permits Missouri courts to recognize other bases of jurisdiction consistent with fairness and substantial justice in international commerce or relations.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; six mandatory personal-jurisdiction bases and permissive recognition of other fair international jurisdictional bases verified.
